stimulus: A survey telescope's image archive held 1,200 images at the start of an observing run. On each night of the run, the telescope adds a minimum of 80 images and a maximum of 150 images to the archive. Let $T$ be the total number of images in the archive after 10 nights of the run.
explanation: Over 10 nights the telescope adds at least $10(80) = 800$ and at most $10(150) = 1{,}500$ images. You add the starting 1,200 images to both ends: $1{,}200 + 800 = 2{,}000$ and $1{,}200 + 1{,}500 = 2{,}700$. 'Minimum' and 'maximum' both include their endpoints, so $2{,}000 \le T \le 2{,}700$.

A.why: You scaled both ends correctly to 800 and 1,500, but you stopped there. Those are only the images added during the run. You forgot to add the 1,200 images already in the archive.

B.why: You scaled only one end of the range. Your upper bound is correct, but your lower bound adds a single night's 80 images to 1,200 rather than 10 nights' worth.

D.why: You added one night's range to the starting 1,200 and never multiplied by the 10 nights. That gives the archive size after one night, not after ten.

stimulus: A polymer strip that is 50 millimeters long is stretched in a tensile test. To pass, the strip must stretch to more than 12 percent beyond its original length but no more than 30 percent beyond its original length. Let $L$ be the stretched length, in millimeters, of a strip that passes.
explanation: 12 percent of 50 is 6 and 30 percent of 50 is 15, so the stretched length is $50 + 6 = 56$ at the low end and $50 + 15 = 65$ at the high end. 'More than' is strict, so the left sign is $<$. 'No more than' includes the endpoint, so the right sign is $\le$. This gives $56 < L \le 65$.

A.why: 6 and 15 are how far the strip stretches, not its stretched length. You need to add them to the original 50 mm.

B.why: Your bounds are right, but you used $\le$ at the low end. 'More than 12 percent' is strict, so a strip that stretches to exactly 56 mm fails the test.

D.why: You added 12 and 30 straight to 50 as if they were millimeters. You needed to take 12 percent and 30 percent of 50 first.

stem: Which of the following could be the total number of buckets of soil that have been sifted at the end of the shift?
stimulus: At an excavation site, 25 buckets of soil had already been sifted before a shift began. During the shift, each of 6 volunteers sifts at least 14 buckets but fewer than 20 buckets.
explanation: Together the 6 volunteers sift at least $6(14) = 84$ buckets and fewer than $6(20) = 120$ buckets. Adding the 25 buckets already sifted gives $109 \le T < 145$. Of the choices, only 132 falls inside this range.

A.why: You added one volunteer's minimum of 14 to the 25 buckets already sifted. You didn't multiply by the 6 volunteers.

B.why: 84 is the volunteers' combined minimum for the shift. You left out the 25 buckets sifted before the shift, and 84 is below the true minimum of 109.

D.why: 145 is the upper end of the range, but 'fewer than 20' per volunteer is strict. The total must be less than 145, so it can't equal 145.

stimulus: On a regional map, 1 centimeter represents 2.5 kilometers. A cartographer measures a winding road on the map several times and reports that its map length is no shorter than 6 centimeters and no longer than 9 centimeters. Let $r$ be the actual length of the road, in kilometers.
explanation: Multiply both ends of the map range by the scale: $6(2.5) = 15$ and $9(2.5) = 22.5$. 'No shorter than' means $\ge$ and 'no longer than' means $\le$, so both endpoints are included: $15 \le r \le 22.5$.

A.why: Your endpoints are correct, but you made both signs strict. 'No shorter than' and 'no longer than' include the endpoints, so 15 km and 22.5 km are both possible.

B.why: You divided the map lengths by 2.5 when you should have multiplied. Each centimeter stands for 2.5 km, so the real length must be larger than the map length.

C.why: You added 2.5 to each end when you should have multiplied by 2.5. A scale factor is applied by multiplying.

stimulus: A paleobotanist counts fossil pine pollen grains in a lake-sediment core. In the layer being studied, each cubic centimeter of sediment contained more than 120 pine pollen grains but at most 180 pine pollen grains. The paleobotanist takes 5 cubic centimeters of this sediment and adds 40 modern pine pollen grains as a reference marker before counting. Let $G$ be the total number of pine pollen grains in the prepared sample.
explanation: The 5 cubic centimeters hold more than $5(120) = 600$ and at most $5(180) = 900$ fossil grains. Adding the 40 marker grains to both ends gives 640 and 940. 'More than' makes the left end strict, and 'at most' includes the right end: $640 < G \le 940$.

A.why: Your bounds are right, but you swapped the strictness at the two ends. 'More than 120' is strict, so the left sign is $<$. 'At most 180' includes 180, so the right sign is $\le$.

B.why: 600 and 900 count only the fossil grains. You forgot to add the 40 marker grains to both ends.

D.why: You added the 40 marker grains to the range for a single cubic centimeter and never multiplied by the 5 cubic centimeters in the sample.

stem: Which inequality represents this situation, where $P$ is the worker's total pay, in dollars, for the week?
stimulus: A staffing agency places a warehouse worker for one 5-day week. Each day the worker works at least 6 hours but no more than 9 hours, at $\$22$ per hour. The worker also receives a one-time $\$40$ signing bonus that week.
explanation: Over 5 days the worker works between $5(6) = 30$ and $5(9) = 45$ hours, inclusive. Pay for those hours runs from $22(30) = 660$ to $22(45) = 990$ dollars. The $\$40$ bonus is paid once, so you add it to both ends: $700 \le P \le 1{,}030$. Both bounds are inclusive because 'at least' means $\ge$ and 'no more than' means $\le$.

B.why: You scaled the hours correctly but left out the $\$40$ bonus. It belongs in the total, so it has to be added to both ends of the range.

C.why: This is one day's pay with the bonus added: $22(6)+40$ to $22(9)+40$. You didn't multiply the hours by the 5 days in the week.

D.why: You added the bonus to every day and then multiplied by 5, so you counted it five times. The bonus is paid once, so you add it after scaling, not before.

stem: Which inequality represents all possible values of $d$, the depth, in centimeters, of the trench at the end of the 4 days?
stimulus: An archaeology team has already dug a test trench to a depth of 40 centimeters. On each of the next 4 days, the team deepens the trench by more than 15 centimeters but less than 25 centimeters.
explanation: Over 4 days the team removes more than $4(15) = 60$ and less than $4(25) = 100$ centimeters. Adding the 40 centimeters already dug to both ends gives $100 < d < 140$. Both ends are strict because the stem says 'more than' and 'less than'.

B.why: Your bounds are right, but 'more than' and 'less than' are strict. A depth of exactly 100 or exactly 140 centimeters can't happen, so the symbols must be $<$, not $\le$.

C.why: This is the soil removed over the 4 days, not the total depth. You still have to add the 40 centimeters that were already dug to both ends.

D.why: You scaled only the upper end. The lower bound $55$ is $40 + 15$, which is one day's minimum. You have to multiply both ends by 4 before adding 40.

stem: Which inequality represents all possible values of $t$?
stimulus: In a linguistics study, each participant records a 15-second spoken introduction and then reads a list of 30 words aloud, taking $t$ seconds per word. For a recording to be usable, its total length must be at least 90 seconds and at most 150 seconds.
explanation: The total length is $15 + 30t$, so $90 \le 15 + 30t \le 150$. Subtract 15 from all three parts to get $75 \le 30t \le 135$. Then divide by 30 to get $2.5 \le t \le 4.5$. Both ends are inclusive because 'at least' and 'at most' mean $\ge$ and $\le$.

B.why: You divided 90 and 150 by 30 without taking off the 15-second introduction first. The introduction counts toward the total length.

C.why: You added 15 to each bound when you should have subtracted it. That gives $105 \le 30t \le 165$ in place of $75 \le 30t \le 135$.

D.why: You subtracted the 15 seconds from the lower bound only. You have to apply every step to both ends, so the upper bound is $(150-15)/30 = 4.5$, not $150/30$.

stem: Which of the following could be the total mass of fish, in kilograms, that the seal eats over these 7 days?
stimulus: A marine biologist caring for a 75-kilogram harbor seal plans its diet so that each day the seal eats a minimum of 4% and a maximum of 6% of its body mass in fish. The seal's body mass stays the same for 7 days.
explanation: Each day the seal eats between $0.04(75) = 3$ and $0.06(75) = 4.5$ kilograms, inclusive. Over 7 days the total $F$ satisfies $7(3) \le F \le 7(4.5)$, or $21 \le F \le 31.5$. Of the choices, only 30 falls in that range.

A.why: This is the most the seal can eat in a single day. You stopped before multiplying by the 7 days.

B.why: You multiplied only the upper end by 7, which gives $3 \le F \le 31.5$. The minimum also applies every day, so the weekly lower bound is 21 and 15 is too small.

D.why: You read 4% and 6% as 4 and 6 kilograms per day, which gives $28 \le F \le 42$. The percents are of the seal's 75-kilogram body mass, so the real maximum is 31.5 kilograms.

stem: Which inequality represents all possible values of $D$, the total length of the performance, in minutes?
stimulus: A movement of a string quartet contains 480 beats, and the score directs that it be played at a steady tempo of at least 96 but no more than 120 beats per minute. One performance also includes a 30-second unmetered cadenza.
explanation: The playing time is $480$ divided by the tempo. At 120 beats per minute that is $480/120 = 4$ minutes, and at 96 beats per minute it is $480/96 = 5$ minutes, so the faster tempo gives the shorter time. The cadenza adds 30 seconds, or $0.5$ minute, to both ends: $4.5 \le D \le 5.5$.

B.why: This is only the time spent playing the 480 beats. You left out the 30-second cadenza, which adds 0.5 minute to both ends.

C.why: You added the cadenza as 30 minutes. It lasts 30 seconds, which is 0.5 minute.

D.why: You added the cadenza to the lower bound only. The cadenza is part of every performance, so it has to be added to the upper bound as well.
